verdict.rationale: SES's sandbox mode (docs-13,14,22,41) is designed exactly for this: new accounts are restricted to sending only to verified identities, letting developers test send flows without reaching real inboxes, and 'you can use all of the features of Amazon SES' while sandboxed. However, the evidence doesn't confirm a dedicated mailbox simulator or explicit test-only API keys that always fire deterministic bounce/complaint/delivery events without needing pre-verified recipients, which is the more CI/agent-friendly pattern developers expect. Missing for 10: documented simulator addresses (e.g. success@simulator.amazonses.com) or dedicated test API keys, and confirmation that sandbox mode fires the full event webhook suite without manual verification steps.
